assigned.title: Watchlist becomes usable: an add control and a list
assigned.acceptance: A person can add a title to their watchlist and see the list. The API and its mutation rules are complete, tested and reviewed -- including the conflict semantics in packages/persistence/src/watchlist-mutation.ts -- and nothing renders them. REQUIRED: the add control appears on the title screen and on a catalog card, and reflects state optimistically while remaining correct when the write is refused. REQUIRED: the resolution vocabulary the API already returns (accepted plus a reason, not a boolean ok) is surfaced honestly; a refused write must not render as a success, which is the shape of defect the harnesses in this repository have caught four times.

52 of those are this task's four new suites:

  watchlist-page-data.test.ts  13  the pure selection and all four branches of the server-side load,

ONE EXISTING TEST WAS CHANGED AND IT WAS STRENGTHENED, NOT RELAXED.
`components/continue-watching/continue-watching-ui.test.tsx` asserted `expect(html).not.toContain
("<button")` on a resume card. PW-0304 mounts the My List toggle inside `CatalogCard`, so that line
began failing for a card that was behaving correctly -- it asserted an implementation (this card has
no buttons) rather than the property its own comment states (start over NAVIGATES, it does not
submit). Replaced by three assertions, each sharper than what it replaces: the href and the text are
now matched as ONE anchor element rather than as two independent `toContain`s; no `<button>` whose
text is "Start over"; and the one button a resume card may carry is named by its `data-testid`, so
the file states what it tolerates instead of tolerating any button. The surface amendment and this
reasoning were recorded as `task.definition_changed` before the file was touched.

A DEFECT THE UNIT LAYER DID NOT CATCH, RECORDED HERE BECAUSE THIS GATE IS WHY. `watchlistRequest`
sent `POST`; the route exports `PUT` and `DELETE` and answers 405 to a POST.
`watchlist-state.test.ts` asserted `POST` right beside the implementation, so this gate was green
while the control could not add anything. The e2e gate found it. `watchlist-ui.test.tsx` now reads
`app/api/v1/watchlist/[contentId]/route.ts` and asserts that every verb `watchlistRequest` can
produce is one that module exports, with a non-vacuity check on the extraction.

NOT A GATE ON THIS TASK AND NOT CLAIMED AS ONE: `npm run lint` (12/12, exit 0) and
`npm run repo:validate` (passed) were also run. `npm run format:check` fails on 538 files and did so
before this task; nothing here changed that and it is not asserted either way.

announces "Choose a profile first.", and leaves the list empty; and on the PostgreSQL run the list
page renders a stored entry, removes it, and the row is gone after a reload.

assigned.title: Series navigation and the next episode
assigned.acceptance: A viewer can move through a series without going back to the catalog. Today every season of a series renders as one flat stack on the title page, with no season selector, no per-episode progress and no way to reach the next episode. REQUIRED: season navigation that does not lose the viewer's place. REQUIRED: per-episode watched and in-progress state from the progress API. REQUIRED: a next-episode affordance at the end of playback, honouring the SAME per-episode rights gate the episode list already applies -- an autoplay that skips the rights check would be the rights breach PL-0703 was opened for, in a new place. REQUIRED: the next-episode selection rule is a pure function with its own tests, not logic inside a component, because 'what plays next' is exactly the kind of decision this project requires to be reconstructible.

recommended.title: Offline, degraded and error states a desktop application needs
recommended.acceptance: The application behaves honestly when the network, the backend or the sidecar is unavailable. There is no offline handling of any kind today -- no navigator.onLine, no service worker, no offline banner, no retry-on-reconnect. THIS MATTERS MORE ON THE DESKTOP THAN IT DID ON THE WEB: docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 8 accepts that an offline desktop cannot resolve playback at all, and requires that failure be surfaced as an honest unavailable outcome rather than an empty candidate list -- so the UI half of that ruling is this task. REQUIRED: a network-state signal and a visible degraded mode that names what is unavailable. REQUIRED: recovery on reconnect without a manual reload. REQUIRED: the sidecar being down is a DISTINCT state from the backend being down and from the network being down, because the three have different remedies and collapsing them produces a support burden. REQUIRED: no state invents content; an offline home shows what it has and says so.
